content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List available project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any ageing/transparency-related documents. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates and their 10-year-equivalent humidity transparency losses; identify which candidates satisfy the hard requirement of ≤10% transparency loss."},{"id":"s2","description":"For each candidate that satisfies the ageing requirement, run simulate_separation at a coarse grid of allowed thicknesses: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm. Record the resulting pion/kaon separation values numerically for comparison."},{"id":"s3","description":"Identify the best-performing candidate/thickness region from the coarse scan. For each viable candidate with competitive performance, run additional simulations at finer thickness points around its best coarse thickness within the 1–6 cm range, using increments no larger than 0.5 cm."},{"id":"s4","description":"Compare all simulated separations among only candidates passing the humidity ageing requirement. Select the radiator and thickness with the highest pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c, ensuring the thickness is within 1–6 cm and the transparency loss is ≤10%."},{"id":"s5","description":"Record the final selected radiator index/name, thickness in cm, transparency loss percentage, and achieved separation in sigma as numeric values where possible, and provide these results to the reporting module for the final recommendation."}]}
